betterCitation: Dōgen, Shōbōgenzō, Genjōkōan, section 6, Enlightenment Unfolds, pp. 35 to 39 (trans. Robert Aitken and Kazuaki Tanahashi, 1999)
reason:
REFUTED on the source line, which carries no locator at all, and on a note that fixes the wrong problem. The wording itself survived every attack I made on it, so this is a fix rather than a kill.

THE WORDING IS SOUND, AND I CHECKED IT AT THE SOURCE THE CREDIT NAMES. I fetched both the terebess parallel page the verifier used and, behind it, the gnusystems Genjokoan concordance it reprints, which is where the credit line actually comes from. That credit reads: 'Actualizing the Fundamental Point, tr. Robert Aitken and Kazuaki Tanahashi. Revised at San Francisco Zen Center, and later at Berkeley Zen Center; published (2000) in Tanahashi, Enlightenment Unfolds (Boston: Shambhala), 35-9. Earlier version in Tanahashi 1985 (Moon in a Dewdrop), 69-73.' In the text carrying that credit the passage runs 'Firewood becomes ash, and it does not become firewood again. Yet, do not suppose that the ash is after and the firewood before.' So the proposed sentence is verbatim in the printing the source names, both translators are correctly credited, and the note's insistence on restoring Aitken is right and well founded. I also checked the year, because the page the verifier leaned on says 2000 and the proposal says 1999: Open Library records Enlightenment Unfolds, Shambhala, first published 1999, with printings in 1999 and 2000. 1999 is defensible and I am not refuting on it.

WHAT BREAKS IT, FIRST. Rule 4 requires a locatable citation carrying work and book, chapter, letter, section or line, or edition and page. The proposed source line, 'Dōgen, Shōbōgenzō, Genjōkōan, in Enlightenment Unfolds (trans. Robert Aitken and Kazuaki Tanahashi, 1999)', gives a work, a fascicle and a book and then stops. There is no section and no page anywhere in it. The locator exists, but it is sitting in the evidence block where no reader will ever see it, and the card prints the source line. The house has already set the form for this exact fascicle: month 04 ships 'Dōgen, Shōbōgenzō, Genjōkōan, section 4, Moon in a Dewdrop, p. 70 (trans. Robert Aitken and Kazuaki Tanahashi, 1985)'. A second Genjōkōan line in the same year with a weaker locator than the first is a visible regression. I confirmed the section number is internally consistent before recommending it: in the concordance numbering 'To study the buddha way' and 'Firewood becomes ash' are two segments apart, so on the scale the house used in month 04, where that passage is section 4, the firewood passage is section 6, which is what the verifier's evidence says. betterCitation puts section 6 and the page span into the source line; it is 127 characters, leads with the name, carries no dash and no straight quote.

WHAT BREAKS IT, SECOND, AND MATTERS MORE AT SIX IN THE MORNING. Taken alone, 'Firewood becomes ash, and it does not become firewood again.' asserts precisely the reading Dōgen spends the next sentence forbidding: the very next words are 'Yet, do not suppose that the ash is after and the firewood before.' The isolated sentence is a flat statement of one way irreversibility, which is the opposite of the fascicle's teaching that firewood abides in the phenomenal expression of firewood and ash in the phenomenal expression of ash. The brief keeps a standing rule for lines of this shape, that a real quotation which is nearly always misread ships only with its gloss (its entries for Sartre and for Nietzsche's madman say so, and the second speaker trap says the note must carry what is being reported). The note here is entirely about translator credit and says nothing about the sense. Two clean ways out, either acceptable: ship both sentences together, 'Firewood becomes ash, and it does not become firewood again. Yet, do not suppose that the ash is after and the firewood before.', which is verbatim in the same printing and self correcting on the card; or keep the one sentence and put Dōgen's own correction into the note in place of half the translator history. As it stands the card teaches the misreading and the note does not catch it, and left alone it will read as bleak in a month that must not be.

EVERYTHING THAT SURVIVES. shipped.js on the exact line: shipped [], near [], dogen at 1 of 3 for the year (month 4), cap 3, not banned, so a second Dōgen is inside the cap, though the editor should notice that both lines would come from the same five pages of the same fascicle in the same translation. Scope is clear: Genjōkōan is 1233 and is Dōgen's own composition, not scripture, and the house has already ruled it in. Tag Philosophy matches month 04. The quotation ends in a full stop and holds no quote marks. Publishable. And it is the right theme for August, once it is allowed to say what Dōgen meant by it.
